7:  ## 2. OVERVIEW
8:  
9: -### Why This Skill Exists
10: -
11: -An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
12: -
13:  ### What It Does
14:  
15:  cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
16:  
17:  It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.

7:  ## 2. OVERVIEW
8:  
9: -### Why This Skill Exists
10: -
11: -An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
12: -
13:  ### What It Does
14:  
15:  cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
16:  
17:  It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.

429: +  --format json \

.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/multi-provider/variant-levels-comparison.md:21:On OpenCode 1, the cli-opencode skill defaults to `--variant high` because routine dispatches benefit from elevated reasoning effort (per SKILL.md §3 and `references/cli-reference.md` §5). On OpenCode 2 the same effort rides on the model id (`-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high`); this comparison keeps the model fixed on that default on purpose, so each version compares the same provider route. If the variant flag is silently ignored or the levels leave reasoning depth unchanged, the skill default loses its value and operators have no real way to dial cost vs depth. This test proves the variant flag is functional by comparing `minimal` vs `high` (the skill's own verified default for `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, not an unverified `max` value, which is not enumerated for this provider anywhere in the current skill) for the same prompt and confirming the response byte count and depth differ materially.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/multi-provider/variant-levels-comparison.md:29:- Objective: On OpenCode 1, confirm `--variant minimal` and `--variant high` produce materially different response depth for the same prompt on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, proving the variant flag drives provider reasoning effort. On OpenCode 2 the same comparison rides on the model selector (`-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#minimal` versus `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high`). `high` is used as the upper comparison point because it is the one variant value this skill's own docs (SKILL.md §3 default invocation, `references/cli-reference.md` §5) vouch for on this provider, while `max` is not enumerated for deepseek anywhere in the current skill and its acceptance is unverified.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/parallel-detached/parallel-detached-session.md:23:Use case 2 is the documented exception to the self-invocation guard. The guard MUST trip on in-OpenCode runtime AND the prompt MUST include parallel-session keywords for the dispatch to be permitted (per ADR-001 + SKILL.md §1 "When NOT to Use" exception clause). If the dispatch is refused even with valid parallel-session keywords, every ablation, worker farm and parallel research workflow regresses. If the dispatch is permitted without parallel-session keywords, the safety story collapses. This test exercises the legitimate use case 2 path with the keywords included.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/agent-routing/general-agent-default.md:21:`general` is an OpenCode built-in, not a project-local agent file under `.opencode/agents/`, and the current cli-opencode contract explicitly forbids passing it at the top level: `opencode run --agent general` is rejected by OpenCode 1 (OpenCode 2.0.32 accepts it, and the rule still forbids it) (SKILL.md §3 "The `--agent` flag" note and hard rule `no-bare-agent-general`). The default agent already runs whenever `--agent` is omitted, which is what every ordinary dispatch should do. If the unflagged path silently fails or produces degraded behavior, the entire default-routing contract collapses and every other scenario that relies on the unflagged shape inherits the failure.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cli-invocation/dir-flag-working-directory.md:21:On OpenCode 1, the cli-opencode default invocation always pins `--dir <repo-root>` to avoid CWD ambiguity (per SKILL.md §3 "Default Invocation"). If `--dir` is silently ignored or overridden by the caller's CWD, cross-repo dispatch (use case from CO-029) silently breaks and the dispatched session loads the wrong project's plugins. This is the foundational test that proves `--dir` pins the CWD inside the dispatched session.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cli-invocation/base-non-interactive-invocation.md:21:Every other scenario in this playbook builds on this baseline. 14: # cli-opencode
15: 
16: > Give any external AI assistant the project's full runtime in one dispatch: every plugin, skill and registered MCP server, plus parallel detached sessions for ablation and worker farms.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | One-shot dispatch into the project's full plugin, skill and MCP runtime, plus parallel detached sessions and cross-AI handback |
25: | **Invoke with** | "delegate to opencode", "opencode run", "parallel detached", "cross-ai handback" or auto-routing on OpenCode keywords |
26: | **Works on** | Any external runtime (Claude Code, OpenCode, raw shell) and from inside OpenCode for parallel detached workers |
27: | **Produces** | Structured JSON event streams, code changes with full project context, parallel research sessions and cross-AI handback results |
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
36: 
37: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.
38: 
39: ### Why This Skill Exists
40: 
41: An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
42: 
43: ### The Dispatch Surface
44: 
45: | Capability | What the skill can operate |
46: |---|---|
47: | **One-shot full-runtime dispatch** | `opencode run` loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there |
48: | **Parallel detached sessions** | separate session ids and state in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database for ablation suites and worker farms |
49: | **Cross-AI handback** | bridges the dispatch result back into the caller's spec folder through the Memory Handback |
50: | **Provider and model surface** | reaches every configured provider catalog through `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster |
51: | **Agent delegation** | routes to project-local agents under `.skilled/agents/` with the primary-versus-subagent caveats in `references/agent-delegation.md` |
52: 
53: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version. OpenCode 1 is supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. QUICK START
58: 
59: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
60: 
61: ```bash
62: command -v opencode2 || command -v opencode
63: ```
64: 
65: If nothing prints, install with `brew install opencode` (macOS) or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`. On the recommended layout `opencode` is OpenCode 2 and `opencode1` is the OpenCode 1 fallback. A machine with only OpenCode 1 answers to `opencode`.
66: 
67: **Step 2: Run the provider auth pre-flight.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: opencode providers list
71: ```
72: 
73: Expected when configured: a table of providers with status and default indicators. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), the skill asks before falling back rather than substituting a model you did not approve.
74: 
75: **Step 3: Run the default dispatch.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the expected version:
79: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
80:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
81:   --format json \
82:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
83:   </dev/null
84: ```
85: 
86: ```bash
87: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
88: opencode run \
89:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
92:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
93:   </dev/null
94: ```
95: 
96: The two versions do not always list the same providers, so on OpenCode 2 check that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first. OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider on this machine, and the `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent on OpenCode 1, so `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the single default on both versions.
97: 
98: You get structured JSON events streamed to stdout as the session runs: `step_start`, `tool_use`, `text` and `step_finish`, every one carrying a `sessionID`, with the reply text in `text` events. The `</dev/null` is mandatory on non-interactive runs on both versions, because the hang is observed on OpenCode 1 and unverified on OpenCode 2. 110: ```

113:

14: # cli-opencode
15: 
16: > Give any external AI assistant the project's full runtime in one dispatch: every plugin, skill and registered MCP server, plus parallel detached sessions for ablation and worker farms.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | One-shot dispatch into the project's full plugin, skill and MCP runtime, plus parallel detached sessions and cross-AI handback |
25: | **Invoke with** | "delegate to opencode", "opencode run", "parallel detached", "cross-ai handback" or auto-routing on OpenCode keywords |
26: | **Works on** | Any external runtime (Claude Code, OpenCode, raw shell) and from inside OpenCode for parallel detached workers |
27: | **Produces** | Structured JSON event streams, code changes with full project context, parallel research sessions and cross-AI handback results |
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
36: 
37: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.
38: 
39: ### Why This Skill Exists
40: 
41: An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
42: 
43: ### The Dispatch Surface
44: 
45: | Capability | What the skill can operate |
46: |---|---|
47: | **One-shot full-runtime dispatch** | `opencode run` loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there |
48: | **Parallel detached sessions** | separate session ids and state in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database for ablation suites and worker farms |
49: | **Cross-AI handback** | bridges the dispatch result back into the caller's spec folder through the Memory Handback |
50: | **Provider and model surface** | reaches every configured provider catalog through `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster |
51: | **Agent delegation** | routes to project-local agents under `.skilled/agents/` with the primary-versus-subagent caveats in `references/agent-delegation.md` |
52: 
53: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version. OpenCode 1 is supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. QUICK START
58: 
59: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
60: 
61: ```bash
62: command -v opencode2 || command -v opencode
63: ```
64: 
65: If nothing prints, install with `brew install opencode` (macOS) or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`. On the recommended layout `opencode` is OpenCode 2 and `opencode1` is the OpenCode 1 fallback. A machine with only OpenCode 1 answers to `opencode`.
66: 
67: **Step 2: Run the provider auth pre-flight.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: opencode providers list
71: ```
72: 
73: Expected when configured: a table of providers with status and default indicators. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), the skill asks before falling back rather than substituting a model you did not approve.
74: 
75: **Step 3: Run the default dispatch.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the expected version:
79: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
80:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
81:   --format json \
82:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
83:   </dev/null
84: ```
85: 
86: ```bash
87: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
88: opencode run \
89:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
92:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
93:   </dev/null
94: ```
95: 
96: The two versions do not always list the same providers, so on OpenCode 2 check that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first. OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider on this machine, and the `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent on OpenCode 1, so `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the single default on both versions.
97: 
98: You get structured JSON events streamed to stdout as the session runs: `step_start`, `tool_use`, `text` and `step_finish`, every one carrying a `sessionID`, with the reply text in `text` events. The `</dev/null` is mandatory on non-interactive runs on both versions, because the hang is observed on OpenCode 1 and unverified on OpenCode 2. Do not pass top-level `--agent` by default: `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` are subagents that route through a primary path (or, for `ai-council`, through its own `/deep:ai-council` command). Top-level `--agent` is only conditionally allowed for primary agents such as `plan` or `orchestrate` after `opencode run --help` confirms acceptance. When a specific agent profile matters, describe it in the prompt body instead, as this example does.
99: 
100: **Step 4: Spawn a parallel detached session (inside OpenCode only).**
101: 
102: > **Do not pass `--share`.** OpenCode 2 `run` has no such flag. On OpenCode 1.19.3 (fallback) it is a hidden, deprecated flag that prints "Session sharing has been discontinued" and publishes nothing.
103: 
104: ```bash
105: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
106: opencode run --port 4096 \
107:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
108:   "Run a parallel research branch for the approved spec folder." \
109:   </dev/null &
110: ```
111: 
112: On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
113: 
114: The session runs under its own session id in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database (`opencode.db`, `storage/`, `snapshot/`), inspectable independently via `opencode export <sessionID>`. On OpenCode 2 there is no share URL because `run` has no share flag, and on OpenCode 1.19.3 `--share` is a deprecated no-op that publishes nothing.

15: # OpenCode CLI - Agent Delegation
16: 
17: How cli-opencode routes dispatches to specialized OpenCode agents via the `--agent <slug>` flag. The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes it.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: OpenCode agents are markdown files under `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`. Each file's frontmatter pins the model, tool permissions, system prompt, and behavioral constraints. When `opencode run --agent <slug>` is invoked, the dispatched session inherits all of that.
26: 
27: The cli-opencode skill exposes the project's full agent roster. The calling AI selects the right slug based on the task type. The agent then shapes the dispatched session: different model, different tool permissions, different system prompt.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - A dispatch needs a role other than the default agent.
32: - The task type picks the slug: codebase exploration, documentation generation, code review, root-cause debugging, or a command-owned research or review loop (§4 maps each to its invocation shape).
33: 
34: ### Discovery commands
35: 
36: | Command | Purpose |
37: |---------|---------|
38: | `opencode agent list` | List all registered agent slugs across project + user scopes |
39: | `opencode debug agent <slug>` | Print resolved frontmatter and system prompt for a slug |
40: | `opencode debug skill <slug>` | Print skill resolution if the agent loads one |
41: 
42: OpenCode loads `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, which in this repository links to `.skilled/agents/`, where the files are edited. On OpenCode 1.19.3, user-level agents fall back from `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`), `~/.opencode/` and `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` when the project file is missing. Which of those OpenCode 2.0.32 reads is unverified. The `debug agent` subcommand prints the merged result so the calling AI can confirm which file the dispatch will load.
43: 
44: ### Orchestration principle
45: 
46: The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes the task. The calling AI always validates and integrates the output.
47: 
48: This separation of concerns is load-bearing for the cli-opencode skill: the calling AI owns the task graph and the integration step, while the dispatched OpenCode session owns the per-task execution under the agent's tool permissions and system prompt.
49: 
50: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
55: 
56: ### Invocation pattern
57: 
58: On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:
59: 
60: ```bash
61: # OpenCode 1 only
62: opencode run \
63:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
64:   --agent <slug> \
65:   --variant max \
66:   --format json \
67:   --dir /repo \
68:   "<prompt>"
69: ```
70: 
71: ```bash
72: # OpenCode 2
73: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
74:   --agent <slug> \
75:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
76:   --format json \
77:   "<prompt>"
78: ```
79: 
80: - **Effort:** On OpenCode 1, the `--variant max` flash pin is the cli-opencode default for cross-AI dispatches on the flash default, and `--variant high` stays the generic effort for non-pinned models. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#<level>` suffix.
81: - **Working directory:** On OpenCode 2 the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`.
82: - **Provider check:** On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`).
83: - **Model precedence:** The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2.
84: - **Frontmatter effects:** OpenCode 2.0.32 routes a slug the same way and registers the agent's mode, permissions and temperature from its frontmatter. With the `openai-compatible` provider package, the only one tested, it does not send that temperature to the provider, so an agent's `temperature` has no effect there (OpenCode 1 sends it for a primary agent through the same package). Whether it applies those permissions during a run is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.
85: - **Pinned-model test:** No repo agent pins a model, so whether a pinned model beats `-m` on OpenCode 2.0.32 is untested.
86: 
87: ```text
88: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
89:   |
90:   |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug
91:   |-- Constructs opencode run command with --agent <slug> flag
92:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
93:   |
94:   v
95: opencode run --agent <slug> (EXECUTOR ENTRY)
96:   |
97:   |-- Resolves .opencode/agents/<slug>.md frontmatter
98:   |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules
99:   |-- Loads project plugins, skills, and MCP servers
100:   |
101:   v
102: OpenCode Session (AGENT EXECUTION)
103:   |
104:   |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints
105:   |-- Streams JSON events (step_start, tool_use, text,
106:   |    step_finish) to the calling AI
107:   |-- Honors LEAF agent restrictions (no nested dispatches, read-only)
108:   |
109:   v
110: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR — RESULT HANDBACK)
111:   |
112:   |-- Parses the JSON event stream
113:   |-- Validates agent output quality
114:   |-- Integrates findings into the parent workflow
115:   |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Conductor rules
119: 
120: 1. The calling AI always **decomposes** complex tasks before delegating to a single agent.
121: 2. The calling AI always **validates** OpenCode output before integrating.
122: 3. The calling AI never **blindly forwards** user requests to OpenCode without picking the right agent.
123: 4. OpenCode agents operate within their declared tool-permission boundaries. LEAF agents may not write files or dispatch sub-agents.
124: 5. If an agent returns low-quality output, the calling AI retries with refined instructions or selects a different agent.
125: 6. Each `opencode run` invocation is **stateless** by default. Include all necessary context in the prompt or use `--continue` / `--session <id>` for explicit continuation.
126: 7. The calling AI surfaces the JSON event stream to the operator when relevant, especially `tool_use` events.
127: 
128: ### Orchestration boundaries
129: 
130: | Concern | Owner |
131: |---------|-------|
132: | Task selection and decomposition | Calling AI |
133: | Agent slug selection | Calling AI |
134: | Prompt construction (RCAF / TIDD-EC / etc.) | Calling AI |
135: | Model and variant selection | Calling AI (agent frontmatter may pin) |

32: - Installing OpenCode 1.19.4 alone or side by side, the fallback path for users who have not updated

422: ## 7. MEMORY HANDBACK
423: 
424: cli-opencode dispatches that produce evidence for a `/speckit:save` continuity write MUST include the Memory Epilogue at the end of the prompt. The dispatched session adds `MEMORY_HANDBACK_START` / `MEMORY_HANDBACK_END` delimiters around a structured JSON payload that the calling AI extracts and feeds to `generate-context.js`.
425: 
426: The full Memory Handback Protocol is shared with cli-claude-code and cli-opencode. See SKILL.md Section 4 (RULES) for the canonical 7-step procedure. The same JSON normalization (camelCase / snake_case aliases) and save gates apply.
427: 
428: ---
429: 
430: ## 8. SINGLE-DISPATCH DISCIPLINE
431: 
432: **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
433: 
434: - **Default**: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the work to return, verify outputs exist.
435: - **Kill only the dispatch THIS skill started**: capture its PID at launch (`opencode run ... & OC_PID=$!`) and SIGKILL that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup. (A backgrounded `opencode run &` is not a process-group leader, so a group kill would miss it. Kill the captured PID directly.)
436: - **Never blanket-kill**: never a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` pattern (see Rule 5), which kills operator-owned sessions too.
437: - **Before the next dispatch**: only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
438: - **Deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole session at start, and iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
439: - **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.

159: Every mode is idempotent, and every step prints its rollback line. The helper never runs a rollback, an uninstall or an upgrade, and it changes no data file: when `opencode.db` exists and `opencode-v1.db` does not, `both` prints the copy command above instead of running it. It writes the links and the launcher only after both npm installs succeed. If the second npm install fails, the first stays installed and nothing else is written. Rerunning `both` completes the layout.
160: 
161: `check` reads the binaries from `$HOME` rather than from the caller's `PATH`, so it reports the layout even when the two disagree [documented: the helper contract].

163: ### Official v2 Channels
164: 
165: The official v2 channels as of 2026-10-18 [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)].
166: 
167: The v2 binary is named `opencode`, the same as v1's [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)], so none of these channels solves side-by-side on its own. The `opencode1` launcher is still required.
168: 
169: - `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash`
170: - `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`
171: - `npm install -g @opencode/cli`
172: - bun, pnpm, yarn and Vite+ install paths
173: - AUR package `opencode-beta`
174: - `mise use -g opencode`. mise 2026.10.9 and later install OpenCode 2 under the name `opencode`, while older mise versions install OpenCode 1 [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)]. A mise upgrade alone can therefore move a user from v1 to v2 with no explicit choice, so pin the version when you need to stay on v1.
175: 
176: ### Homebrew Is v2-Only and Exclusive
177: 
178: `brew install opencode` installs a v2 `opencode` on the default `PATH` [confirmed: `brew info --json=v2 opencode` reports stable `2.0.32`, and the formula tracks the v2 repository].
179: 
180: There is no `opencode@1` formula and no versioned formula at all [confirmed: `versioned_formulae` is an empty list]. Homebrew therefore cannot supply the v1 leg of a side-by-side layout, and a Homebrew v2 collides with an npm v1 on the `opencode` name. One of the two becomes invisible depending on `PATH` order. Treat Homebrew as a v2-only, exclusive channel. Use it when you want only v2, and use the two-prefix npm layout when you want both.

# OpenCode CLI - Self-Invocation Guard (ADR-001)

Layered detection contract for refusing a circular cli-opencode dispatch when the calling agent is already running inside OpenCode, in both bash and python pseudocode form.

Document the full three-layer self-invocation detection contract behind ADR-001 — env-var lookup, process-ancestry probe, and state lock-file probe — so `SKILL.md` §2 (SMART ROUTING) can carry a short summary and pointer instead of the full code.

### When to Use

Read this when implementing, auditing, or debugging the self-invocation guard referenced from `ROUTER.md` §3 and from `integration-patterns.md` §5 (decision tree + exact refusal message).

134:> **Registered command dispatch (`--command`, OpenCode 1 only)**: slash-command text inside a `run` message is NOT expanded. OpenCode 2 has no `run` flag for a registered command. On OpenCode 1 (fallback), use `opencode run --command <family>/<name> [flags] "<args>"`. Full semantics: `references/cli-reference.md` §4.
138:On OpenCode 2, run `opencode models --standalone` filtered for the `<provider>/` prefix (2.0.32's `models` takes no provider argument). 209:11. **Run the Provider Auth Pre-Flight once per session** (see §3 Provider Auth Pre-Flight). Cache the configured-providers list. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), ASK the user. Never silently substitute the model. If a later dispatch returns an auth error, invalidate the cache and rerun the pre-flight before retrying.
240:    - Full procedure: [`references/integration-patterns.md`](./references/integration-patterns.md) §8.
251:    - Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.opencode/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc.). Never hardcode one runtime.
282:OpenCode-specific Memory Epilogue template: see [assets/prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md) §14.

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```

68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). 202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23:

26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95:

97: 
98: ```markdown

100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---

111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!

136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.

154: - [Second trigger]

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES

238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints

245: - Root cause analysis required

247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes

252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

258: - Overview and "When to Use"

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.

290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```

306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"

311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

322:

327: 2. [Action 2]

359: \```

363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---

# Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines

Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Location & Naming

**Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`

**Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension

| ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
|---------------|-----------------|
| `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
| `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
| `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
| `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |

### When to Create Assets

**Create an asset file when:**
- Templates users apply repeatedly
- Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
- Multiple examples of same pattern exist
- Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
- Template variations for different scenarios

**Keep in SKILL.md when:**
- Content <30 lines
- Tightly coupled to workflow logic
- Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
- Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)

---

## 2. ASSET FILE TYPES

### Template Files
**Purpose**: Provide copy-paste starting points for common tasks

**Naming**: `[content-type]-templates.md`
- Example: `frontmatter-templates.md`, `structure-templates.md`

**Structure**:
- One template per section
- Include field descriptions
- Show complete examples
- Explain when to use each template

**Use cases**:
- Document templates (SKILL.md, commands, knowledge files)
- Configuration templates (YAML, JSON)
- Code templates (functions, classes, modules)

### Reference Files
**Purpose**: Provide lookup tables, decision trees, or reference data

**Naming**: `[topic]-reference.md`
- Example: `emoji-reference.md`, `validation-reference.md`

**Structure**:
- Tables or lists for quick lookup
- Decision matrices
- Classification systems
- Standards and conventions

**Use cases**:
- Emoji selection guides
- File type classifications
- Validation rule sets
- Naming conventions

# Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines

Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Location & Naming

**Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`

**Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension

| ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
|---------------|-----------------|
| `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
| `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
| `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
| `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |

### When to Create Assets

**Create an asset file when:**
- Templates users apply repeatedly
- Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
- Multiple examples of same pattern exist
- Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
- Template variations for different scenarios

**Keep in SKILL.md when:**
- Content <30 lines
- Tightly coupled to workflow logic
- Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
- Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)

A: When you are inside OpenCode and want a second session with its own state and session id. Common patterns are an ablation suite across sessions, a worker farm for parallel research and a cross-repo research branch. On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md). The prompt must contain explicit parallel-session keywords or the self-invocation guard blocks the dispatch.

**Q: Why no top-level `--agent`?**

A: OpenCode 2 accepts `--agent general`. OpenCode 1 (fallback) treats named agents like `general` as subagents and will not run them at the top level: it prints a warning, falls back to the default agent and exits 0, so the flag does not select the requested agent. The default agent already covers the general case. For a specific profile, describe the role in the prompt body.

**Q: Why does a non-interactive dispatch hang without `</dev/null`?**

A: OpenCode reads stdin at startup before session creation. When stdout and stderr are redirected to files, stdin stays open and the process waits forever. Appending `</dev/null` provides an immediate EOF so the dispatch continues.

**Q: Which model do I pick?**
